clue.text: African shrub used for hot drink:

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
tea is a hot drink

explanation.surface: A plant from Africa whose leaves are brewed for a hot cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a flowering shrub native to southern Africa, the national flower of South Africa.

clue.text: Crime of traitor with no time for logical argument

indicators.note: with no means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: treason is the crime a traitor commits

explanation.surface: Treachery that leaves no time for rational debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' removes T from TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the faculty of logical thought, and also a justification or argument.

clue.text: Ancient Rome's enemy — how he flies!

definitions.text: Ancient Rome's enemy — how he flies!

parts.words: Ancient Rome's enemy — how he flies!
parts.note: time, everyone's enemy, put in the Latin of ancient Rome, with an exclamation about how fast it passes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Rome's enemy' suggests Hannibal or Carthage; it is time, the universal enemy, named in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proverb means time flies, here time is cast as the enemy of the Romans' language.

clue.text: French illustrator turning up in a city's airport

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rome is the city

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: A French artist appears at a city's airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means read from the bottom, so the illustrator's name comes out as EROD; 'in' then slots it into the city after the article.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an airfield, an old word for an airport.

clue.text: Man who briefly may be highly regarded at the seaside

definitions.text: Man who briefly may be highly regarded at the seaside

parts.words: Man who briefly may be highly regarded at the seaside
parts.note: a man's name whose short form is a lofty coastal rock face, something looked up to at the seaside

explanation.walkthrough: The short form of this name is Cliff, and a cliff is a high feature, literally looked up at, on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name usually shortened to Cliff, which is also a tall rock face by the sea.

clue.text: A crimson resin from below the crater

indicators.note: from below in a down clue means reading upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: crimson is red
lac is a resin secreted by insects

explanation.surface: A red resin oozing from beneath the volcano's crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' reverses A RED LAC to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large volcanic crater, formed by collapse after an eruption.

clue.text: Unsuitable apparatus initially installed in home gym

indicators.note: installed in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: in means at home
PT, physical training, is gym

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of apparatus

explanation.surface: Unsuitable equipment has been put into a home gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home gym' looks like one place, but it splits into two pieces, home and gym; 'initially' takes just the opening letter of apparatus, and 'installed in' sets it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not apt, ill-suited or inappropriate.

clue.text: Certified.OK by the doctor for bout?

definitions.meaning: passed as healthy after a medical examination
a sudden attack, as of coughing or temper

explanation.definitionFit: Fit means medically healthy, and a fit is a sudden bout of illness or emotion.

clue.text: Island, one north of a country that declared independence

indicators.note: north of in a down clue means the pieces before it sit above the a

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An island lies north of a nation that broke away.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodesia made a Unilateral Declaration of Independence from Britain in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe, famously declared independence unilaterally from Britain in 1965.

clue.text: Short dance ethical in castle

indicators.note: short means the word for dance loses its final letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
moral means ethical

explanation.surface: A brief dance with moral standards held in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter from BALL to give BAL. Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the Scottish castle used by the British royal family as a summer residence.

clue.text: Fighting division deprived of leader

indicators.note: deprived of leader means the first letter of the word for division is dropped

parts.note: a faction is a division within a group

explanation.surface: A military division that has lost its commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of leader' removes the F from FACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is combat, as in soldiers seeing action, so it means fighting.

clue.text: Cask kept in bar for stout

indicators.note: kept in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rod is a bar
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A barrel of stout kept behind the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer that suits cask and bar, but it is the adjective meaning plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund and stout are synonyms for plump, rounded in build.

clue.text: Rum not bland, surprisingly sweet -

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A strange claim that rum is not bland but surprisingly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges RUM NOT BLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnt almond is a sweet: an almond coated in caramelised sugar.

clue.text: Giraffe roams around to find food.

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A giraffe wanders about looking for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'around' as the giraffe wandering about; it actually signals the rearrangement of the two words before it, with 'to find' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fromage frais is a soft fresh cheese, eaten as food.

clue.text: English 'chaps expert and the French not beyond -redemption?

parts.note: men are chaps
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert
le is French for the

explanation.surface: English fellows, skilled, and the French are not past saving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emendable can be corrected or improved, so it is not beyond being put right.

clue.text: Sole trader who is noted for her coarse language?

definitions.meaning: someone who sells fish such as sole, punning on a one-person business

definitions.text: who is noted for her coarse language?
definitions.meaning: a loud woman known for vulgar, abusive speech

explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife sells fish, and the word also means a coarse-mouthed, shrill woman.

clue.text: Grannie slept uneasily — family member who could do with more help?

definitions.text: family member who could do with more help?

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters toss and turn into a new order

explanation.surface: Grandma has a restless night, a relative who needs a bit more support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' rearranges GRANNIE SLEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent raising children alone is a family member who could well use extra support.

clue.text: A former archbishop's very quiet in praise

indicators.note: in means the musical marking goes inside

parts.note: William Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury
pp, pianissimo, is very quiet in music

explanation.surface: A former archbishop is very hushed while giving praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The archbishop's 's stands for 'has': he has the musical marking 'in', placed straight after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap or praise someone.

clue.text: Unskilled workers face 500 being sacked

parts.note: men are workers

indicators.note: being sacked means the letter for 500 is removed

parts.note: a dial is a clock face
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: Unskilled staff facing the loss of 500 jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being sacked' drops D (500) from DIAL, leaving IAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Menial work is lowly and needs little skill.

clue.text: Redstart with exceptional speed returning

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters of with are out of their usual order
returning means the word for speed is read backwards

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: A small bird flying back at remarkable speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges WITH to WHIT; 'returning' turns PACE into ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitecap is an old country name for the redstart, a small songbird with a white forehead.

clue.text: Dishonourable man leading soldiers in small group.

indicators.note: leading in a down clue means the first piece comes above the second

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: A rogue at the head of a small band of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained people, especially in an army or party.

clue.text: Sorrow, dropping our fellows in the old tomb

indicators.note: dropping means the letters of our are removed from the word for sorrow

parts.note: dolour is grief or sorrow
taken as written
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Grieving at the ancient burial site, having lost our friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping our' removes OUR from DOLOUR, leaving DOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric stone structure, an ancient tomb of upright stones under a capstone.

clue.text: Spurned Jack's companion, shortly meeting another boy

indicators.note: shortly means the word for the companion is cut by its final letter

parts.note: Jill goes with Jack in the nursery rhyme
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Jill, rejected by Jack, soon takes up with a different lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims JILL to JIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jilted is to be rejected by a lover, so spurned.

clue.text: What's in cigarettes accounting for half the duty

indicators.note: accounting for half the means taking the first half of the word for duty

parts.note: a tariff is a customs duty

explanation.surface: The smoking chemical makes up half the tax on cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: TARIFF halved gives TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is the sticky residue in tobacco smoke, a harmful constituent of cigarettes.

clue.text: Intend to eat sort of apple, coming back after a meal fit for gods

indicators.note: after means what comes back follows the a
coming back means that combination is read backwards
to eat means the word for intend takes the apple inside it

parts.note: aim means intend
sorb is the fruit of the service tree, also called the sorb apple

explanation.surface: Planning to munch an apple on the way back after a heavenly feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts the apple inside the aim, giving AISORBM; 'coming back' turns that into MBROSIA, and 'after' sets it behind the clue's opening article.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was the food of the gods, conferring immortality.

clue.text: Before death characters reconvened in brief support

indicators.note: before means the shuffled letters come ahead of the word for death
the characters of the word brief are reconvened, that is reassembled in a new order

parts.note: end means death

explanation.surface: Before dying, the cast reassembled briefly to offer support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before death' looks like a time phrase but places one piece ahead of another; 'characters reconvened in' rearranges the letters of brief to BEFRI.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to act as a friend to them and give them support.

clue.text: Phantoms perform in a story from the east

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
from the east in an across clue means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a lie is a story, a falsehood
do means perform

explanation.surface: Ghosts appear in a tale from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'from the east' means right to left, so the article and story read backwards as EILA; 'in' puts perform's synonym inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidola is the plural of eidolon, a spectre or phantom image.
